children: The Bank of Japan is likely to hike or intervene in the coming weeks, given the yen's underperformance, RBC Capital Markets' Abbas Keshvani says in commentary. The yen has underperformed over the last month, undoing most of BOJ's intervention in recent months. A yen recovery will require an aggressive hiking cycle, but the central bank is unlikely to jeopardize growth in such a manner, he says. "Instead, they will likely hike enough to prevent excessive yen weakness until stability in JGBs next year can usher in a currency recovery," he adds. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
